examples.scenario: Best PROJ operation needs a grid that is missing, so runtime silently selects a lower-quality operation.
examples.reason: ONLY_BEST must fail when the best required grid is unavailable.

examples.scenario: A vertical CRS conversion succeeds through a ballpark operation.
examples.reason: Ballpark vertical operations can have unknown large error and do not perform the required datum shift.

examples.scenario: PROJ_DATA differs between the primary run and replay.
examples.reason: Grid availability changes candidate operations and must be frozen for reproducibility.

examples.scenario: Network grids are enabled in one run but unavailable in another.
examples.reason: Network/grid state is part of the executable transformation environment.

examples.scenario: A null grid allows zero shift outside the intended grid coverage.
examples.reason: A zero shift outside the approved model region can conceal a missing transformation.

examples.scenario: Two overlapping grids are listed in different order and produce different coordinates.
examples.reason: PROJ uses grid order when multiple grids cover a point.

examples.scenario: A survey-period vertical grid is replaced by a newer grid without reconciliation.
examples.reason: Survey-period transformation/geoid lineage must be preserved or explicitly reconciled.

examples.scenario: OSGM15 model standard error is treated as total parcel elevation error.
examples.reason: Transformation-model error excludes LiDAR, GNSS and checkpoint components.

examples.scenario: A generic WGS84 coordinate is passed into a high-accuracy GB transformation as if it were precise ETRS89.
examples.reason: Reference-frame realization is required for precision provenance.

examples.scenario: Pixel corner coordinates are used as the pixel centre.
examples.reason: GDAL defines the centre of the upper-left pixel at pixel/line 0.5,0.5.

examples.scenario: A georeferenced point is converted to the wrong column/line because the position CRS was implicit.
examples.reason: Coordinate space and resulting column/line must be recorded together.

examples.scenario: Bilinear interpolation is used for a terminal point sample from the native DTM.
examples.reason: Interpolation produces a derived value rather than the exact native cell value.

examples.scenario: Nearest sampling uses a fractional coordinate but the selected cell index is not logged.
examples.reason: Replay needs the exact source pixel supporting the terminal value.

examples.scenario: A VRT pixel is sampled without recording which underlying file contributed.
examples.reason: Contributing raster identity is part of terminal provenance.

examples.scenario: A composite DTM value is accepted although the target location has a timestamped native DTM.
examples.reason: Composite values can be resampled and mix survey epochs.

examples.scenario: DSM and DTM have similar values at an open field, so DSM is allowed as fallback.
examples.reason: Surface and terrain models remain semantically different even when values happen to match.

examples.scenario: A point cloud exists but no matching historical DTM raster does, so a new raster is generated and treated as canonical.
examples.reason: Derived point-cloud rasterization requires separate lineage and cannot silently replace the provider raster.

examples.scenario: The same rounded elevation is reproduced with a different PROJ operation and different source pixel.
examples.reason: Transform operation, grid set and source pixel must also match.

examples.scenario: A programme ±15cm threshold is reported as the exact uncertainty of the parcel height difference.
examples.reason: Target-specific survey and processing components must be bound before a parcel uncertainty is reported.

examples.scenario: Numeric height difference is published while canonical point and runner outputs remain absent.
examples.reason: Terminal numeric output stays fail-closed until canonical inputs and executable evidence exist.
